DD.thesis_one_line: Specialty materials maker for water, healthcare, aerospace and construction, now light on debt after two divestitures and priced below what its cash flow can grow.
kill_criteria: Organic sales growth below 2% for two consecutive quarters (2Q'26: +4%).
FY26 adjusted EPS guidance cut below the $7.17 low end, or FY27 initial guidance implying adjusted EPS growth under 5%.
Consolidated net debt (10-Q total debt less cash and cash equivalents) above 2.0x trailing operating EBITDA (now about 0.8x).
New PFAS or legacy settlement that adds more than $500m to DuPont's accrued share beyond the $125m (NC) and $188m (NJ) liabilities at June 30, 2026, or Qnity failing to honour its 44% allocation.
Transaction-adjusted FCF conversion below 80% for FY26 (1H'26 is about 127% in 2Q).
key_adverse_facts: Most of the 2026 adjusted EPS jump (FY26 guide $7.17-$7.32 vs FY25 $5.04 post-split) is lower interest, lower tax and fewer shares, not operating growth; 2Q26 interest expense $41m vs $84m, tax rate 28% vs 69%
PFAS: Sep 9 2026 NC settlement of $455m over 15 years shared under the 2021 MOU; DuPont booked about $125m in discontinued ops in Q2 2026 and carries a $188m NJ liability; Qnity reimburses 44%
Healthcare & Water EBITDA margin down 30 bps to 30.1% in 2Q26; weakness in the Middle East and construction end-markets
Short clean track record as new DuPont: only two post-spin quarters on a continuing-operations basis
data_conflicts: d4 fcf_yield 10.3% uses Yahoo TTM FCF $1,835m including discontinued operations; continuing-ops owner FCF about $950m (5.3%)
Yahoo trailing EPS $2.33 / P/E 56.5x mixes discontinued ops; the triage WATCH rested on this distortion
EPS printed pre-split in releases before Aug 2026; 1-for-3 reverse split effective June 24 2026 (converted x3 here)
DD.confidence_in_thesis: medium: primary filings show beats and raises for three quarters and a de-levered balance sheet, but the EPS base is partly financing-driven and PFAS is an open tail

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DV12 restatement: Ke 9.5% (5.17% Treasury + 1.056 Blume beta x 4.14%) and after-SBC FCF $890m imply 6.7% 10-year FCF growth vs the 5.5% base (base path worth about $122.7 a share, 7% below $131.71); the earlier 3.7% used Ke 8.5% and pre-SBC FCF. Price is roughly in line with base, with no margin of safety.

AMGN.thesis_one_line: Large biotech with fast-growing newer medicines and a promising obesity drug, but priced slightly above what slowing profit growth and eroding older drugs can deliver.
kill_criteria: Non-GAAP operating margin below 42% in any quarter (range over the last five quarters: 42.8% in Q4'25 to 48.4% in Q2'26).
FY26 non-GAAP EPS guidance cut below the $22.30 low end, or FY27 guide midpoint under $23.50.
Total debt less cash above 3.0x trailing EBITDA (consolidated, 10-Q balance sheet; now about 2.5x) or FCF below $8bn on a trailing-four-quarter basis.
Prolia plus Enbrel plus Otezla combined net sales falling more than 25% year over year for two quarters (Q2'26: Prolia -32%, Otezla -21%, Enbrel -4%, combined about -21%).
Any amendment to the Item 1.05 cyber 8-K disclosing material financial impact, regulatory penalties or a class action above $500m.
key_adverse_facts: Non-GAAP EPS +4% in Q2 2026 on +10% revenue ($6.29 vs $6.02); cost of sales 19.6% of product sales vs 17.7%
Jul 31 2026 8-K Item 1.05: material cybersecurity incident with proprietary data and patient health information exfiltrated; investigation ongoing
Prolia -32% (biosimilars), Otezla -21%, Enbrel net price -22% under IRA price setting; Otezla price setting from 2027; MFN pricing actions
Debt $57.3bn vs equity $11.7bn (consolidated); $4.0bn notes issued Feb 2026; Kyowa Kirin collaboration terminated (Jan 30 2026)
data_conflicts: Triage '+52% forward EPS growth' compares forward non-GAAP EPS $24.45 with trailing GAAP EPS $16.12; like-for-like non-GAAP growth is about +5% (FY26 midpoint $22.90 vs $21.84) and +6-7% for FY27
Yahoo trailing P/E 25.7x is GAAP, forward 17.0x is non-GAAP; GAAP FY26 guide $15.80-$17.08 vs non-GAAP $22.30-$23.50 (about $6/share acquisition amortization)
ROE 75% in b1 reflects low book equity after buybacks, not unusual profitability
AMGN.confidence_in_thesis: medium: cash generation and guidance raises are solid, but price, cyber incident and legacy erosion cap conviction

FICO.thesis_one_line: The FICO credit score owner earns huge margins, but 2026 growth came from one mortgage price rise now under attack, and debt funds its buybacks.
kill_criteria: Scores segment revenue below $400m in any fiscal quarter (Q3 FY26: $458.9m).
Consolidated total debt (10-Q balance sheet, current maturities plus long-term debt) divided by trailing-twelve-month GAAP EBITDA above 4.5x, or any covenant amendment or waiver disclosure.
FY27 initial non-GAAP EPS guidance below the FY26 guide of $42.43, or FY27 guidance midpoint implying revenue growth under 0%.
Software ARR growth below 5% year over year (June 30 2026: +10%) or platform net retention below 120% (now 148%).
A regulator or the GSEs setting a mortgage score price, a cap or an effective default to VantageScore that cuts FICO mortgage origination royalty revenue by more than 25% on a run-rate basis.
key_adverse_facts: About 98% of Q3 FY26 revenue growth was Scores, driven by mortgage origination unit price (Scores +$134.6m of +$137.8m); revenue growth decelerating from +39% to +26%; implied Q4 revenue about $652m (-3% sequentially)
Total debt $5.58bn (consolidated, Jun 30 2026) vs $3.06bn at Sep 30 2025; stockholders' deficit $4.1bn; covenant max leverage 4.5x to Dec 30 2026 then 4.0x; GAAP debt/EBITDA about 4.4x

FHFA: all GSE-approved lenders may use VantageScore 4.0 since Sep 9 2026 (fhfa.gov); after the cutoff, on Sep 29 2026, FHFA announced a single pricing grid and FICO fell about 20% premarket (secondary source)
Live Sherman Act Section 2 antitrust claim against FICO survived dismissal (10-Q)
data_conflicts: Triage cited a Sep 4 FHFA directive ending the monopoly; FHFA page shows Sep 9 2026 availability to all lenders, Classic FICO still approved, no retirement date, tri-merge still required
d4 forward P/E 16.3x and Street FY27 EPS $53 predate the Sep 29 news and carry -2.6% 90-day revisions
Post-cutoff price about $598 is from secondary press and not verified against a primary source
FICO.confidence_in_thesis: low: earnings power is proven but the forward mortgage revenue path and covenant headroom are uncertain

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Reverse DCF at $863.09 implies 5.7% 10-year FCF growth against my 3.8% base (base path value about $750 per share). At the post-cutoff price near $598 implied growth would be 0.8% (below base), so the verdict is sensitive to price.
